name: Christian corporatism
summary: Christian corporatism holds that society is an organic body in which employers and workers of each industry or profession should cooperate in vocational groups, in place of class struggle, under a state that directs and supports rather than absorbs. It defends private property with a social duty, a family wage and wide ownership of small property, and rejects both liberal individualism and socialism, resting this third course on Christian morals and the Church.
scope: The Catholic corporatism of Rerum novarum (1891) and Quadragesimo anno (1931), the two texts the scholarship (Vieira de Sousa) names as the core of its teaching, with Heinrich Pesch's solidarism behind them. Answers rest on what those two encyclicals themselves state. Quadragesimo anno's description of Italy's syndicates (paragraphs 91-95) is a report with reservations, not the ideology's own programme. The Austrian Ständestaat, which scholarship links to the doctrine, is not used as the ideology's record: the sources read do not show its practice as part of what the ideology holds. It excludes Protestant corporatism, Mussolini's corporate state and postwar neo-corporatism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Rerum novarum 37 says it is the duty of the public authority to prevent and punish injury and to protect every one in the possession of his own.

bound-labor.rationale: Leo XIII treats labour as personal and the worker as owed a living wage and dignity, which excludes bondage.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 78-80 laments that only individuals and the State remain once intermediate associations are lost and makes lesser groups the bearers of subsidiary function, so dealing with the people without intermediary bodies is rejected.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rerum novarum 19 says capital cannot do without labour nor labour without capital, and Quadragesimo anno 81 asks the state to promote harmony between industries and professions.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rerum novarum 19 calls the notion that class is naturally hostile to class a great mistake and says nature ordains harmony between them, and Quadragesimo anno 112 condemns communism's unrelenting class warfare.

collective-farming.rationale: Rerum novarum 9 and 15 say land worked by a person's labour becomes his own and reject common ownership.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Rerum novarum 15 says the main tenet of socialism, community of goods, must be utterly rejected, and communities holding their property in common are that tenet.

corporate-influence.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 105-108 says concentrated economic power struggles to control the state, which matches complaints of corporate influence.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Rerum novarum 14 says extreme necessity should be met by public aid and 37 that the mass of the poor must chiefly depend on the assistance of the State, though neither sets a general guarantee.

decide-locally.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 79-80 sets subsidiarity, leaving to smaller bodies what they can do, though corporatism organises by vocation and nation rather than by locality alone.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 112 condemns communism's unrelenting class warfare and 120 says no one can be at once a good Catholic and a true socialist.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 58 says the distribution of goods must be brought into conformity with the common good, condemning the huge disparity between the few exceedingly rich and the propertyless, so justice is not judged by process alone.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 118 speaks of man living in society under an authority ordained of God.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rerum novarum 33 says that as regards the State the interests of all, high or low, are equal and the workers are citizens by the same right as the rich, though it also says the poor have a claim to especial consideration (37).

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rerum novarum 17 says unequal fortune follows necessarily from natural unequal condition, rejecting levelling.

family-wage.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 71 requires a wage sufficient to support the worker and his family, and Rerum novarum 45 says it must keep a frugal worker.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Rerum novarum 42 treats a woman's fitness for home work as natural, so adherents see sex roles as grounded in nature.

harm-principle.rationale: Rerum novarum 36 says the community's interest requires that a high standard of morality prevail in public and private life and that religion be obeyed, so state action is not limited to preventing harm to others.

independent-unions.rationale: Rerum novarum 49-52 holds workingmen's unions to be natural societies and says public authority may forbid only associations whose purposes are evidently bad, unlawful or dangerous to the State.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rerum novarum 13-14 and 50 give families and associations rights of their own, and Quadragesimo anno 45 stresses the social character of property.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 53 quotes Leo XIII that the wealth of nations originates from the labour of workers, but 53 also says natural resources come first and 55 rejects the claim that all products and profits belong to workers by right.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rerum novarum 9 and 13 defend land and inheritance as private property earned by labour.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Rerum novarum 6 and 9 defend individual ownership of land one has worked.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pius XI says free competition has destroyed itself and that economic life must be ruled by social justice and charity, though private enterprise stays.

more-religion-public.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 129 says only a return to Christian life and institutions will heal human society, and Rerum novarum 16 and 36 hold that no solution succeeds apart from religion and that it is in the community's interest that religion be obeyed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 46 warns against the twin rocks of individualism and collectivism, 109 says free competition has destroyed itself, and 120 says no one can be at once a good Catholic and a true socialist.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rerum novarum 33 and 37 require the state to actively look after workers and shield the poor, far beyond defence and property.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rerum novarum 52 says laws only bind when they are in accordance with right reason, so legal status alone creates no duty.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 50 says those with superfluous income are bound by a very grave precept to give alms.

person-over-state.rationale: Rerum novarum 35 says the State must not absorb the individual or the family, which should have free action so far as consistent with the common good, and 7 grounds the individual's rights in his nature.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rerum novarum 37 says the poor, lacking resources, deserve the special protection of the state.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rerum novarum 32 and 37 make it the duty of the public authority to prevent and punish injury and protect every one in the possession of his own, so replacing state courts with private companies contradicts it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Leo XIII says capital needs labour and labour capital and rejects the Marxist reading, though he condemns defrauding workers of wages.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rerum novarum 6 holds that every man has by nature a right to own property, and Quadragesimo anno 49 says the state may regulate its use but not abolish it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 45-49 holds that ownership has an individual and a social character and that public authority may define its duties for the common good, but not abolish the right; it does not say property is justified only so far as it serves the common good.

religion-illusion.rationale: Rerum novarum 16 holds that no practical solution to the workers' condition is found apart from religion and the Church, and 24 treats religion as the source of true worth, not as an illusion.

separate-church-state.rationale: Rerum novarum 36 counts it among the interests the public authority must serve that things be carried on in accordance with God's law and that religion be obeyed, and 16 says no practical solution is found apart from religion and the Church, which excludes strict separation.

single-common-good.rationale: Pius XI calls for harmonious cooperation under the common good, but accepts distinct group interests in vocational bodies.

socialized-care.rationale: Rerum novarum 14 says paternal authority can be neither abolished nor absorbed by the State and the family has rights of its own, so public services replacing the family are rejected.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rerum novarum 32 makes laws and institutions serve public well-being, binding rulers to a moral order.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Rerum novarum 40 says the working man has interests of the soul which the State must protect, and 36 counts religion and morality among the community's interests.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rerum novarum 32 and 33 say the State exists to serve the common good and that, as regards the State, the interests of all, high or low, are equal, so it is not the instrument of one class.

state-harmful.rationale: Rerum novarum 32 says the foremost duty of rulers is to see that laws and institutions realise public well-being and private prosperity, and 33 and 36 give the public authority duties to protect rights and to step in where the general interest suffers, so abolishing the state contradicts it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Rerum novarum 36 says the community's interest requires that religion be obeyed and 16 that no solution is found apart from religion and the Church, which excludes state promotion of atheism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rerum novarum 36 lists the moderation and fair imposing of public taxes among the things by which a State prospers, so taxation is accepted as just when fair.

total-state.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 79-80 sets subsidiarity, with the state leaving matters to lesser groups, and Rerum novarum 35 forbids the state absorbing individuals or families.

traditional-family.rationale: Rerum novarum 13-14 calls the family a true society prior to the state with its own rights and paternal authority, and Quadragesimo anno 71 ties the wage to family needs.

unions-good.rationale: Rerum novarum calls workers' associations the most important of all associations, though the corporatist ideal replaces class-only unions with mixed vocational bodies.

universal-morality.rationale: Leo XIII appeals to natural right and the common order given by nature and God, which is universal.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Rerum novarum 52 says laws only bind when they are in accordance with right reason, and its note 38 quotes Aquinas that a law deviating from right reason is no law at all.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rerum novarum 20 and 38 tell workers never to resort to violence or disorder and to have nothing to do with men of evil principles who stir revolutionary change, so a disciplined party of revolutionaries leading them is rejected.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 105-109 describes an immense power and despotic economic dictatorship in few hands and says free competition destroyed itself.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 58-61 condemns the gulf between a few rich and the propertyless and wants workers able to acquire property through thrift.

missingStatements.text: A worker's wage should be enough to support the worker and his family.
missingStatements.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 71 requires a wage sufficient to support the worker and his family, and Rerum novarum 45 says it must keep a frugal worker.

missingStatements.text: The state should leave to smaller communities and associations whatever they can do themselves, and step in only to direct and support.
missingStatements.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 79-80 sets out the subsidiary function: larger bodies must not take over what smaller ones can do, and the state directs, watches, urges and restrains.

missingStatements.text: Strikes and lockouts should be forbidden and disputes settled through joint bodies of employers and workers.
missingStatements.rationale: Quadragesimo anno 94 describes the corporative order as one in which strikes and lockouts are not allowed, with disputes handled inside the vocational groups.

notes: Evidence this pass is the full text of Rerum novarum and Quadragesimo anno (Vatican site) and Vieira de Sousa's 2007 scholarly article on Catholic corporatism. The earlier pass's answers that rested on Wikipedia summaries of the Austrian regime or on inference from the doctrine were nulled unless the encyclicals settle the statement; where an answer was kept or changed, its rationale cites paragraphs checked in the saved text. Themes searched in the encyclicals: property and inheritance, wages and the family wage, hours and child and women's labour, strikes and associations, the state's duties and subsidiarity, vocational groups, class, socialism and communism, religion and the Church in public life, charity and the poor, law and obedience, international economic cooperation (paragraph 89 only). The texts are silent on most social issues, criminal justice, immigration, environment, technology, foreign policy and many modern questions, so those are null. Quadragesimo anno 114 (certain kinds of property reserved to the State) and 85-87 (free vocational associations) were read against earlier answers on public ownership and state-recognised bargaining and both were nulled. The uncertainty rule is applied by the validator, not argued here.

keyFigures.role: Author of Rerum novarum, which founded modern Catholic social teaching on class cooperation and workers' associations.
keyFigures.quote: Leo XIII had indicated two paths to the resolution of what Catholics called the 'social question'.

keyFigures.role: Author of Quadragesimo anno, which promoted vocational-group corporatism as an alternative to capitalism and socialism.
keyFigures.quote: Pius XI proposed something more radical
